summary.headline: Max India consolidated revenue rose 90.4% YoY to INR 95.5 crores in Q2 FY27, while EBITDA loss halved to INR 11.4 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR 95.5 crores in Q2 FY27, up 90.4% YoY and 40% QoQ from INR 68.6 crores in Q1. EBITDA loss narrowed to INR 11.4 crores from INR 25.3 crores a year ago and INR 24.9 crores in Q1, a 55% YoY and 54% QoQ reduction. Management attributed the improvement to higher revenue and cost optimisation, while flagging that the assisted senior living (ASL) DM fee income is lumpy and tied to construction-linked collections. Noida Phase 1 handovers accelerated to over 200 units, and AGEasy hit its highest-ever monthly revenue of INR 14.9 crores in September 2026.

segments.name: Residences (ASL DM business)
segments.commentary: Estate 360 is sold out with Q2 collections of INR 28.5 crores and DM fee of INR 2.6 crores; Estate 361 has sold about 263 of 360 units. Management fees across 360, 361 and Noida Sector 150 were INR 17 crores in Q2 and INR 23 crores in H1.

segments.name: Assisted Care (Care Homes)
segments.commentary: Care Home revenue rose to about INR 9 crores from INR 3 crores over 5-6 quarters. Occupancy across all beds was 29% in Q2 vs 26% in Q1, and 4 of 8 care homes are at or above plan. Contribution margin for same-capacity homes improved from -86% to -19%.

segments.name: AGEasy (D2C eldercare products)
segments.commentary: Q2 net revenue was INR 35 crores, with September at a record INR 14.9 crores and exit ARR near INR 180 crores. CM2 improved to -29% in Q2 from -48% in Q1, reaching about -11% in September; ROAS rose to 4.7 from 2.0.

guidance_outlook: AGEasy targeted to reach EBITDA breakeven and marginally positive in Q4 FY27; management said CM2 was trending toward zero, with September at about -11%.
Care Homes expected to reach EBITDA breakeven by end of H1 FY28; management said overall positivity expected by H2 FY28.
Noida Phase 1 remaining handovers expected to finish by end of November 2026, with maintenance charges starting 1 November 2026.

Gross sales value commitment of INR 1,800 crores a year to be met for the next few years, with new Bengaluru (~INR 900 crores, 6.5 lakh sq ft), Dehradun (INR 850-900 crores) and other NCR and South India projects under discussion.
Noida Phase 2 project IRR expected at 15-17%, subject to Noida authority acceptance of the sports-sector resolution plan and building plan revalidation.

Care Home per-unit model: about 4 quarters to reach 40-45% occupancy (unit-level CM positive), 8-10 quarters to reach 60% maturity with 30-32% unit CM and 16-18% EBITDA after HO cost. Management aspires to take ARPOB near INR 9,000 within 12 months.
capex_capacity: Antara Noida community is fully operational; over 200 of 340 Phase 1 units handed over by early November, at 5-6 handovers a day. Recognised revenue on 131 units (127 handovers plus 4 registries).
Care Homes capacity is 485 beds across 8 homes; occupancy on older beds rose from 21% to 36%. Sector 41 Gurgaon at 37% in Q2 and DLF Care Home at 45% within 3 months of launch.
Noida Phase 2 expenses are held in inventory; only Phase 1 Towers 1-3 costs are expensed, which is why Noida shows no loss.
Bengaluru diligence is nearly complete and definitive agreements are being discussed; Dehradun, further Delhi NCR and one South India project are pending commercial closure.
AGEasy has 10 patents (4 granted, 6 filed, including 1 international), up from 6.
demand_pricing: Care Home ARPOB averaged about INR 6,900 in Q2 FY27, up from INR 5,800 six quarters ago; fresh move-ins in September 2026 reached about INR 8,400.
Estate 361 sold about 263 of 360 units, with about 97 units left in the second lot; average sales of about 31 units a month in the last quarter.
Noida Phase 1 was sold at about INR 6,500-7,000 per sq ft; Phase 2 market price is about INR 18,000.
AGEasy online D2C and marketplace gross margin held at 45% in Q2 exit despite logistics cost pressure from the Middle East situation; satisfaction index 82%.
AGEasy reached 11.7 lakh lives served and 1.14 lakh repeat customers; NPS 49 in H1 FY27; over 5 lakh families.

qa_highlights.question: How much of AGEasy's September surge is seasonal versus sustainable, and why did offline revenue jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Ishaan Khanna said 75-80% of the surge is sustainable, with some festive-driven rationalisation expected in October. Offline growth comes from expanded distributor networks built over the last 3 quarters, and Q3 is expected to exceed Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Where will employee costs stabilise, and what drives operational expenses for assisted care?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajit Mehta said employee cost rose from Noida staffing (150+ added) and the labour code and revised PF rules, which were unanticipated. Ajay Agrawal said corporate employee cost is stable, and variable costs rise only with new projects, geographies or care homes. Ankit Kalra said assisted care opex covers care home operations and AGEasy logistics and marketplace commissions.

qa_highlights.question: How is the DM fee revenue recognised?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajay Agrawal said the fee is accrued on collections made by Max Estates, reconciled quarterly, at 9.5% of collections net of pass-through and brokerage, and recognised when the invoice is raised, not at project completion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state ARPOB, and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajit Mehta said annual revenue per bed is INR 22-25 lakh, covering room, nursing, pharmacy and procedures. Ishaan Khanna said the 12-month aspiration is about INR 9,000 per day as clinical cross-sell rises.

qa_highlights.question: Noida accounting: what DM fee was recognised, and why no share of loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajay Agrawal said INR 9.98 crores of DM fee was recognised this quarter (INR 33 lakh in June, the balance in September). Phase 2 costs are kept in inventory, so only Phase 1 project costs are expensed, leaving a marginal gain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for consolidated EBITDA breakeven, and are restructuring plans under way?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AGEasy breaks even in Q4 FY27 and Care Homes by end-H1 FY28, with overall positivity in H2 FY28. Residences were said to be EBITDA-positive over a project cycle. Rajit Mehta said restructuring is being considered for governance and investor reasons but is premature and not yet crystallised.

risks_watch: Lumpy ASL DM fee income tied to collections and construction milestones, which can make quarterly EBITDA swing between loss and profit.
AGEasy gross margin pressure from Middle East-driven logistics costs, and whether September-level revenue holds after festive-season normalisation in October.
Noida Phase 2 depends on Noida authority accepting the sports-sector resolution plan and plan revalidation; Noida collections of about INR 6 crores remain pending bank approvals.
Rising employee costs from the labour code and PF changes, plus new projects, could slow margin progress.
Pending restructuring (possible AGEasy demerger or holding-company changes) with no details yet.
Care Homes occupancy of 29% overall; the remaining care homes have yet to reach plan.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and margin trajectory, with specific operating metrics. Management was cautious and deferred on restructuring, future EBITDA timing and new project commercials, saying disclosures will follow once closed.
key_quotes: On a consolidated basis, a very healthy growth on Y-on-Y and on quarter-on-quarter basis on top line and also the losses have substantially reduced.
The reduction in EBITDA loss alongside revenue growth demonstrate our continued progress towards profitability.
So the more it is trends towards 0 and then eventually positive is when we start seeing EBITDA breakeven.

growth.why: Management guides to a INR 1,800 crore a year gross sales value commitment and AGEasy EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27, backed by Noida Phase 1 handovers (over 200 of 340 units) and Estate 361 sales (about 263 of 360 sold), while new Bengaluru and Dehradun projects remain pending closure and Care Home occupancy is only 29%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: AGEasy CM2 improved from -48% in Q1 to -29% in Q2 and about -11% in September, with breakeven targeted for Q4 FY27; Care Homes contribution margin for same-capacity homes improved from -86% to -19%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Noida Phase 1 handovers finish by end-Nov 2026 and Noida Phase 2 (IRR 15-17%) is approved pending sports-sector resolution; Bengaluru (~INR 900 crores) and Dehradun (INR 850-900 crores) are under diligence but not yet closed, so timing of new capacity is uncertain.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Care Home occupancy rose to 29% from 26% and Estate 361 sells about 31 units a month with about 97 units left; management expects Q3 FY27 AGEasy revenue to exceed Q2's INR 35 crores.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is committed to a INR 1,800 crore a year gross sales value target with Bengaluru and Dehradun projects in advanced diligence and commercial closure, so new project announcements are expected; Care Home utilisation is only 29%, so no capacity-driven capex is needed there.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenue grew 90.4% YoY to INR 95.5 crores and AGEasy hit a record INR 14.9 crores in September, but management has not raised numbers and flagged DM fee lumpiness.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: DM fee income is lumpy and tied to collections (INR 9.98 crores in Q2 Noida fees), Middle East logistics costs pressure AGEasy, and employee costs rose from the labour code and PF changes, so quarterly EBITDA could swing back to loss.

rows.label: AGEasy EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27
rows.why: CM2 improved to -11% in September from -48% in Q1 and management guides to breakeven and marginally positive EBITDA in Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Care Homes EBITDA breakeven by end-H1 FY28
rows.why: Occupancy rose to 29% from 26% and 4 of 8 homes are at or above plan; management expects overall positivity by H2 FY28, though 8-10 quarters to 60% maturity.

rows.label: Pending restructuring (possible AGEasy demerger)
rows.why: Management said restructuring is being considered for governance and investor reasons but is premature and not crystallised, with no details yet.

tone.note: Management was confident on AGEasy's growth, the Q4 FY27 breakeven and Noida handovers, but cautious and deferred on restructuring, Bengaluru/Dehradun commercials and future EBITDA timing; analysts probed AGEasy's September surge sustainability, employee cost rises and DM fee recognition.
